description.sr:
Napiši funkciju `partial(fn, ...preset)` koja vraća novu funkciju u kojoj su prvi argumenti funkcije `fn` već zadati.

Kad se vraćena funkcija pozove, `fn` se poziva sa zadatim argumentima (`preset`), a iza njih idu argumenti trenutnog poziva.

Pravila:
- `partial` sam ne poziva `fn`; `fn` se poziva tek kad se pozove vraćena funkcija
- bez zadatih argumenata vraćena funkcija se ponaša kao `fn`
- vraćena funkcija se može pozivati više puta, a svaki poziv dobija iste zadate argumente
- vraćena funkcija vraća ono što vrati `fn`

Primeri:
```
const greet = (greeting, name) => `${greeting}, ${name}!`;
const hello = partial(greet, 'Hello');
hello('Ana');   // 'Hello, Ana!'
hello('Marko'); // 'Hello, Marko!'

const add3 = (a, b, c) => a + b + c;
partial(add3, 1, 2)(3); // 6
partial(add3)(1, 2, 3); // 6
```
description.en:
Write a function `partial(fn, ...preset)` that returns a new function in which the first arguments of `fn` are already set.

When the returned function is called, `fn` is called with the preset arguments (`preset`), followed by the arguments of the current call.

Rules:
- `partial` itself does not call `fn`; `fn` is called only when the returned function is called
- with no preset arguments the returned function behaves like `fn`
- the returned function can be called many times, and every call gets the same preset arguments
- the returned function returns what `fn` returns

Examples:
```
const greet = (greeting, name) => `${greeting}, ${name}!`;
const hello = partial(greet, 'Hello');
hello('Ana');   // 'Hello, Ana!'
hello('Marko'); // 'Hello, Marko!'

const add3 = (a, b, c) => a + b + c;
partial(add3, 1, 2)(3); // 6
partial(add3)(1, 2, 3); // 6
```

text.sr: `...preset` je rest parametar: skuplja sve argumente posle `fn` u niz `preset`. Taj niz ostaje zapamćen u vraćenoj funkciji (closure).
text.en: `...preset` is a rest parameter: it collects all arguments after `fn` into the array `preset`. That array stays remembered in the returned function (closure).

text.sr:
Vraćena funkcija skuplja nove argumente u `rest`, pa poziva `fn(...preset, ...rest)`: spread raspakuje oba niza jedan za drugim, zadati prvo. Spread svaki put pravi nov spisak argumenata i ne menja `preset`, pa više poziva ne utiče jedan na drugi. `fn` se poziva tek ovde, ne u `partial`.

```
partial(add3, 1, 2)(3):
preset = [1, 2], rest = [3]
fn(1, 2, 3) = 6
```
text.en:
The returned function collects the new arguments into `rest` and then calls `fn(...preset, ...rest)`: spread unpacks both arrays one after another, preset first. Spread creates a new list of arguments every time and does not change `preset`, so several calls do not affect each other. `fn` is called only here, not in `partial`.

```
partial(add3, 1, 2)(3):
preset = [1, 2], rest = [3]
fn(1, 2, 3) = 6
```

note.sr: Strelica funkcija ne menja `this`, pa ova verzija ne podržava metode koje zavise od `this`.
note.en: The arrow function does not set `this`, so this version does not support methods that depend on `this`.

text.sr: Isti potpis: `preset` skuplja unapred zadate argumente.
text.en: The same signature: `preset` collects the preset arguments.

text.sr: Svaka funkcija ima metodu `bind`. `fn.bind(thisValue, ...args)` pravi novu funkciju sa unapred zadatim prvim argumentima: baš ono što se traži. Prvi parametar je vrednost za `this`; ovde je `null` jer `fn` ne koristi `this` (strelice ga ionako ignorišu). Nova funkcija se pravi odmah, a `fn` se ne poziva dok se ona ne pozove.
text.en: Every function has a `bind` method. `fn.bind(thisValue, ...args)` creates a new function with the first arguments preset: exactly what is asked. The first parameter is the value for `this`; here it is `null` because `fn` does not use `this` (arrow functions ignore it anyway). The new function is created right away, and `fn` is not called until it is called.

note.sr: Kratko, ali sakriva ono što se dešava; ručna verzija je jasnija za učenje.
note.en: Short, but it hides what happens; the manual version is clearer for learning.
